This page discusses the "Order the steps" box in the pre-processing workflow diagram below.
Essentially, there are 8 positioning steps you can take to order your sequence of Step calls.
Each position has its own page (e.g. "Missing: impute").

{{< include ../_includes/workflow-diagram.qmd >}}

## Overview of eight steps

| Stage | Position | mlfeatures steps |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Handle missing values | [1. Missing: impute](../four-stages/missing-impute.qmd) | `StepImputeMean`, `StepImputeMedian`, `StepImputeMode`, `StepIndicateNa` |
| | [2. Missing: category levels](../four-stages/missing-category-levels.qmd) | `StepUnknown`, `StepOther` |
| 2. Wrangle | [3. Wrangle: transforms](../four-stages/wrangle-transforms.qmd) | `StepLog`, `StepOrderNorm`, `StepDateFeatures`, `StepDatetimeFeatures` |
| | [4. Wrangle: discretize](../four-stages/wrangle-discretize.qmd) | *none; rarely advisable* |
| | [5. Wrangle: dummy variables](../four-stages/wrangle-dummy-variables.qmd) | `StepDummy`, `StepOneHot`, `StepHoliday` |
| 3. Model prep | [6. Model prep: interactions](../four-stages/model-prep-interactions.qmd) | `StepInteract`, `StepPolynomial`, `StepSplineNatural`, `StepSplineMonotone` |
| | [7. Model prep: normalize](../four-stages/model-prep-normalize.qmd) | `StepNormalize`, `StepRange` |
| 4. Multivariate transforms | [8. Multivariate transforms](../four-stages/multivariate-transforms.qmd) | `StepPca`, `StepPls`, `StepClassDistance` |

Each stage exists so the next one works: handle missing first — impute the
numeric gaps and give missing categorical levels an explicit value — because
every later step wants complete columns, and the guard levels must exist
before the dummy step freezes its vocabulary; wrangle everything into numbers
next; model prep after, so interactions can cross indicator columns with
numerics
and normalize catches the freshly created columns; multivariate transforms
last, because they want the finished, scaled matrix.

## Example: eight steps in action

One recipe on the credit data can fill most of the positions. The first
stages handle missing values and turn everything into numbers, and their
order matters because each step decides what the next one sees: impute
first so nothing downstream meets a null, then give missing and rare levels
a name *before* the dummy step, so its vocabulary includes `"unknown"` and
`"infrequent"` and new data cannot introduce a level it has no column for.

```{python}
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

from mlfeatures import (
    Recipe,
    StepDropZeroVariance,
    StepDummy,
    StepImputeMedian,
    StepInteract,
    StepNormalize,
    StepOther,
    StepPca,
    StepUnknown,
)
from mlfeatures import Selectors as s
from mlfeatures.data import credit

credit_train, credit_validation = train_test_split(
    credit, train_size=0.75, stratify=credit["Status"], random_state=1
)

wrangled = (
    Recipe(data=credit_train, target="Status")
    .add(StepImputeMedian(s.numeric_features()))  # 1. impute
    .add(StepUnknown(s.nominal_features()))  # 2. category levels
    .add(StepOther(s.nominal_features(), threshold=0.05, other_level="infrequent"))
    .add(StepDummy(s.nominal_features()))  # 5. dummy variables
)
wrangled.fit(credit_train)
```

The dummy step's resolved columns include `Job_infrequent`, the pooled
level; `Home`'s few missing and rare values were pooled the same way, into
the level its indicators are measured against. Model prep and the
multivariate transform continue from there. Normalize sits after the interaction step so the new product column
is scaled with the rest, and before PCA, which weights columns by their
variance and would otherwise be dominated by the largest-valued ones.

```{python}
recipe = (
    wrangled.add(StepDropZeroVariance(s.features()))  # filter
    .add(StepInteract(s.col("Income", "Amount"), keep_original_cols=True))  # 6. interactions
    .add(StepNormalize(s.numeric_features()))  # 7. normalize
    .add(StepPca(s.numeric_features(), num_comp=3))  # 8. multivariate
)
fitted = recipe.fit(credit_train)
fitted
```

```{python}
fitted.transform(credit_validation).head()
```

## Filtering-related steps

The ordering is deliberately silent on the filter steps (`StepDropZeroVariance`,
`StepDropNearZeroVariance`, `StepDropCorr`) — [dropping columns](dropping-columns.qmd) is not a stage. In
practice filters run as two passes: after stage 1, to drop dead or redundant
raw columns before effort is spent encoding and scaling them, and again after
the dummy step, where a rare level can produce an all-zero indicator column.

## Alternative perspective: step families

While the eight steps focus on the order that steps tend to be put in, this guide also contains a section called Step Families that organizes steps largely by feature type (e.g. Datetime features).
This is often useful when you already know what step you want, or want to browse steps that return similar types of results.
